doc.title: Feature and Functionality
doc.summary: This document outlines the key features and functionalities of the Digii campus-management platform's Asset Management module. It covers vendor management, asset schema definition (categories and sub-categories), consumable product management, purchase order processing, and asset allotment to departments or members.

prerequisites.name: Asset Management Admin
prerequisites.description: The "Asset Management Admin" admin privilege provides access to the whole asset management module. With this privilege administrators can manage asset schema, vendor details, products and assets etc.

chunks.what_it_does: The Add Vendor feature allows Asset Administrators to create and manage vendor records. It enables asset administrators to capture essential details about vendors — vendor name, vendor type, address, phone number, Vendor Since, and GST (Goods and Services Tax) Number. Vendor name and vendor type are mandatory fields, with at least one vendor type required. Vendor types include Organization, Warranty Provider, Insurance Provider, Re-Sale Buyer, Service Provider, and Seller. Only members with Asset Management Admin privilege can add vendors, while other administrators with specific privileges can link vendors to assets.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Add Vendor feature is crucial for centralized vendor management, allowing asset administrators to maintain a comprehensive record of all external vendors. This simplifies tracking warranties, services, and purchases linked to specific vendors. By associating vendors with assets, asset administration teams can improve asset lifecycle management, ensuring assets are properly supported throughout their lifespan.
how_to_use: Access the Asset Management module with 'Asset Management Admin' privilege.
Navigate to the Vendor Details section.
Initiate the 'Add Vendor' process.
Enter the mandatory fields: Vendor Name and at least one Vendor Type (Organization, Warranty Provider, Insurance Provider, Re-Sale Buyer, Service Provider, or Seller).
Optionally, enter non-mandatory details such as Address, Phone Number, Vendor Since, and GST Number.
Save the new vendor record.
examples: Vendor Name: ABC Stationery Supplies Ltd.
Address: 123 Paper Lane, New York, USA

chunks.why_it_matters: This functionality ensures that vendor information remains accurate and reflects any changes such as updated contact details, business status, or service associations over time.

chunks.what_it_does: The Add user functionality allows the Asset Management Admin to grant access privileges to other members for the Asset Management module. Through this feature, the asset administrator can assign permissions to members based on their roles and responsibilities in managing assets. These permissions can be configured at different levels, including Category and Sub-category, Add, View and Allot access for Product, and Add and View access for Asset.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Add user feature is crucial for maintaining controlled access and ensuring that only authorized individuals can manage or view specific asset-related data. It allows Asset Administrators to assign appropriate roles and responsibilities to members, ensuring accountability and security within the platform.
how_to_use: As an Asset Management Admin, navigate to the Admin Privilege section.
Select the 'Add user' option.
Choose the member to whom privileges will be assigned.
Configure permissions based on Category and Sub-category access.
Set 'Add', 'View', and 'Allot' access for Product.
Set 'Add' and 'View' access for Asset.
Save the privilege settings for the user.

chunks.what_it_does: The Add Category feature allows the Asset Management Admin to create a new asset category individually. When adding a category, the administrator defines key details: Category Name (mandatory, e.g., Electronics, Furniture), Type (mandatory dropdown: Fixed or Consumable), Auto-Create Category ID (mandatory toggle for auto-generating a unique 6-character alphanumeric code or manual entry), and Description (non-mandatory).
chunks.why_it_matters: The Add Category feature is essential for organizing and structuring assets in the Asset Management module. It enables asset administrators to establish a clear and organized asset hierarchy, simplifying management and tracking. By categorizing assets as Fixed or Consumable, this feature ensures different asset groups are managed according to their specific needs. The Category ID provides a unique identifier, preventing duplication and ensuring consistency, and aids in generating category-based reports.
how_to_use: As an Asset Management Admin, navigate to the Asset Schema section.
Select the 'Add Category' option.
Enter the mandatory 'Category Name' (e.g., 'Electronics').
Select the mandatory 'Type' from the dropdown (Fixed or Consumable).
Toggle 'Auto-Create Category ID' to 'Enabled' for automatic generation, or 'Disabled' to manually enter a custom Category ID.
Optionally, provide a 'Description' for the asset category.
Save the new category.

chunks.what_it_does: This feature allows Asset Administrators to add multiple asset categories at once by uploading a CSV (Comma Separated Values) file. The CSV file must include mandatory details like Category Name and Auto-Generate Category ID (true or false). If Auto-Generate Category ID is false, a Category ID must be provided. Other fields include Category Type (Fixed or Consumable) and Description (non-mandatory).
chunks.why_it_matters: The Add Bulk Category via CSV (Comma Separated Values) Upload feature is important for asset administrative teams with large volumes of assets, as it streamlines the categorization process, ensuring efficiency and accuracy. By enabling bulk uploads, it saves time, allowing for faster asset categorization.
how_to_use: As an Asset Management Admin, navigate to the Asset Schema section.
Select the 'Add Bulk Category' option.

Prepare a CSV file with the following columns: Category Name (mandatory), Auto-Generate Category ID (mandatory, 'true' or 'false'), Category ID (if Auto-Generate is 'false'), Category Type (Fixed or Consumable), and Description (optional).
Upload the prepared CSV file.
Confirm the bulk creation of categories.

chunks.why_it_matters: The Edit Category feature is important for maintaining and updating accurate details of the asset categories. It allows administrators to quickly adapt asset classifications without creating new categories or disrupting existing sub-category, product, or asset records.

Locate the category you wish to edit.
Click on the 'Edit' option for that category.
Modify the 'Category Name', 'Category ID', or 'Description' fields as needed.

chunks.what_it_does: The Delete Category feature allows Asset Administrators to remove an existing asset category from the Asset Management module. However, a category can only be deleted if it is not mapped to any subcategory or if all associated subcategories are first deleted. Once these conditions are met, the asset administrator can proceed to delete the category, ensuring that there are no dependencies or linked assets that could be affected by the deletion.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Delete Category feature is crucial for maintaining a clean and organized asset management platform. It ensures that asset categories can be properly removed without disrupting the structure of linked assets or subcategories.
how_to_use: As an Asset Management Admin, navigate to the Asset Schema section.
Locate the category you wish to delete.
Ensure that the category is not mapped to any subcategory. If it is, first delete all associated subcategories.
Click on the 'Delete' option for that category.
Confirm the deletion when prompted.

chunks.what_it_does: The Add Single Sub-Category feature allows Asset Administrators to create a new sub-category under an existing asset category. The admin must select the parent category, enter a mandatory Sub-Category Name (e.g., Laptops, Monitors), and choose whether to Auto-Create Sub-Category ID (a unique 6-character alphanumeric code) or manually enter a custom ID. A non-mandatory Description field is also available.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Add Single Sub-Category feature is essential for creating a more detailed and organized asset classification platform. It allows administrators to break down broad asset categories into more specific groups, improving the efficiency of asset tracking, reporting, and management.
how_to_use: As an Asset Management Admin, navigate to the Asset Schema section.
Select the 'Add Single Sub-Category' option.
Choose the 'Category' under which the sub-category will be added.
Enter the mandatory 'Sub-Category Name' (e.g., 'Pens').
Toggle 'Auto-Create Sub-Category ID' to 'Enabled' for automatic generation, or 'Disabled' to manually enter a custom Sub-Category ID.
Optionally, provide a 'Description' for the asset sub-category.
Save the new sub-category.

chunks.what_it_does: This feature allows asset administrators to define and register individual consumable products under specific categories and sub-categories. Mandatory fields include Category Type, Sub-Category Type, Product Name, Product Code (with an 'Auto Generate' toggle for automatic 6-character alphanumeric code or manual entry), and Unit of Measurement (UOM). Optional fields are Description, Store Location, Reorder Threshold, Handle Expiry for this Product (for tracking expiry dates), and Product Image attachments.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Create Product feature is crucial for maintaining an organized, consistent, and easily traceable inventory of consumable assets within the institution. It establishes a structured catalog of consumables, ensures accurate identification with unique product codes, and improves operational efficiency through automated code generation, expiry tracking, and reorder alerts, helping asset administrators manage stock proactively.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Manage Products' tab under Consumable Asset.
Select 'Create Product'.
Choose the mandatory 'Category Type' and 'Sub-Category Type'.
Enter the mandatory 'Product Name'.
Toggle 'Auto Generate' for Product Code or manually enter a custom code.
Select the mandatory 'Unit of Measurement (UOM)'.
Optionally, add a 'Description', 'Store Location', 'Reorder Threshold', enable 'Handle Expiry for this Product', and upload a 'Product Image'.
Save the new product.
examples: Auto Generate Code: Enabled. Platform generates STN452

chunks.what_it_does: The Bulk Upload feature in the Manage Products tab allows asset administrators to efficiently upload a large number of consumable products into the system using an Excel sheet. The Excel file must include Product Name, Product Code (or 'Auto Generate Code' as true/false), Company Name, Sub-Category Name, Sub-Category Code, and Unit Name. Optional fields are Description, Location Name, Reorder Threshold, and Handle Expiry.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Bulk Upload of Product feature is crucial for institutions managing large quantities of consumable items, offering significant benefits. It enhances efficiency by reducing the administrative burden of manual data entry, minimizes the risk of errors through standardized Excel templates, and provides scalability for managing large and constantly changing inventories in various departments.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Manage Products' tab under Consumable Asset.
Select the 'Bulk Upload - Product' option.
Prepare an Excel file with the following mandatory fields: Product Name, Product Code (or 'Auto Generate Code' as true/false), Company Name, Sub-Category Name, Sub-Category Code, and Unit Name.

chunks.what_it_does: The New Purchase feature allows asset administrators to add detailed purchase information for consumable assets, divided into two sections: Purchase Details and Product Details. Purchase Details include mandatory fields like Vendor, Purchase Order ID (new or existing), Date of Purchase, Invoice No, Date of Invoice, Receipt No, and Date of Receipt, with optional Invoice and Receipt Attachments. Product Details include mandatory Product, Cost Per Unit, and Batch Quantity, with auto-calculated Total Quantity and Total Cost, and an optional Expiry Date if enabled for the product. Multiple products and batches can be added under a single Purchase Order ID.
chunks.why_it_matters: The New Purchase feature, encompassing both Purchase Information and Product Details, is vital for efficient asset management. It ensures accurate tracking of purchases from vendor selection to financial documentation, including invoice and receipt details. The product details section ensures all relevant information about purchased products is tracked accurately, from cost to batch details, helping institutions maintain an organized and up-to-date inventory of consumable assets.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Purchase Details' tab under Consumable Asset.
Select 'New Purchase'.

In Section 1: Purchase Details, fill in mandatory fields: Vendor, Purchase Order ID (enter new or select existing), Date of Purchase, Invoice No (enter new or select existing), Date of Invoice, Receipt No (enter new or select existing), and Date of Receipt.
Optionally, upload Invoice Attachment and Receipt Attachment.
In Section 2: Product Details, select the mandatory 'Product'.
Enter the mandatory 'Cost Per Unit' and 'Batch Quantity'.
If expiry tracking is enabled for the product, select the 'Expiry Date'.
Add multiple products or multiple batches as needed.
Save the new purchase record.
examples: Purchase Details – New Purchase for Stationery
Outcome: The purchase details for A4 Paper Pack are entered
Product Details – Stationery Purchase with Multiple Batches
Total Quantity: 500 sheets - calculated as the sum of batches
Total Cost: Rs.50,000 - calculated by multiplying Total Quantity by Cost Per Unit
Expiry Date: Not applicable as expiry tracking is not enabled
Outcome: The product A4 Paper Pack is added successfully with two batches, with the total cost calculated and batch-specific quantities recorded.

chunks.what_it_does: The Create New Allotment feature enables asset administrators to allot consumable assets to specific departments or members. Mandatory fields include Select Category, Sub-Category, Product, Quantity Allotted, Allotted To (Department or Member), Date of Allotment, Location, and Purpose. Optional fields are Allotment Rule FEFO (First Expired First Out) for prioritizing batches with earliest expiry dates, and Allot Expired Quantity for allowing distribution of expired items under certain conditions.
chunks.why_it_matters: The Create New Allotment feature plays a crucial role in managing the distribution of consumables across various departments and members within the institution. This ensures that consumables are allocated to the right departments or members while considering available stock, expiration dates, and purpose, maintaining better control over inventory levels.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Allotment Tab' under Consumable Asset.
Select 'Create New Allotment'.
Choose the mandatory 'Select Category', 'Sub-Category', and 'Product'.
Enter the mandatory 'Quantity Allotted'.
Specify 'Allotted To' (Department or Member).
Select the mandatory 'Date of Allotment' and 'Location'.
Enter the mandatory 'Purpose' for the allotment.
Optionally, enable 'Allotment Rule FEFO (First Expired First Out)' to prioritize batches with earliest expiry dates.
Optionally, enable 'Allot Expired Quantity' if expired consumables are permissible for allotment.
Save the new allotment record.
examples: Outcome: The A4 Paper Pack is allotted to the Department of Administration, with no expiry tracking or expired products being allocated.
Outcome: The Hydrochloric Acid Solution is allotted to Dr. John Doe, with the platform selecting the batch with the earliest expiry date for allocation.

chunks.what_it_does: The View or Return Link against each allotment record allows asset administrators to manage allotment records efficiently. Clicking this link provides a complete breakdown of allotment details (product, quantity, recipient, purpose, location). If items need to be returned, the 'Return Items Button' reveals a 'Quantity to Return' field. After entering the amount, the 'Process Return' button completes the return, updating inventory and allotment records.
chunks.why_it_matters: The View or Return Link in the Allotment Tab of Consumable Assets allows asset administrators to efficiently manage allotments by accessing detailed information, including product details, quantity allotted, recipient, purpose, and location. If any product needs to be returned, administrators can enter the Quantity to Return and complete the return process. This helps in updating both the inventory and allotment records accordingly.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Allotment Tab' under Consumable Asset.
Locate the specific allotment record you wish to manage.
Click on the 'View or Return Link' associated with that record to see detailed allotment information.
If items need to be returned, click the 'Return Items Button'.
Enter the 'Quantity to Return' in the provided field.
Click the 'Process Return' button to complete the return and update inventory.
examples: Clicking the View or Return Link reveals the allotment details for A4 Paper Pack, showing the quantity allotted, department, and other relevant information.
After clicking the Return Items Button, the administrator enters 10 Packs in the Quantity to Return field.
Clicking Process Return updates the inventory, reducing the total allotted quantity and ensuring accurate stock tracking.
